pairs: No evils will befall one who fears the Lord.
sed in tentatione Deus illum conservabit,
God will preserve him during temptation
Sapiens non odit mandata et justitias,
and will free him from evils.
et non illidetur quasi in procella navis.
A wise man does not hate the commandments and the justices, and so he will not be thrown about violently, like a ship in a storm.
A man of understanding puts his faith in the law of God,
and so the law is faithful to him.
Whoever would resolve a dispute will prepare a word, and so,
having prayed, he will be heard.
The heart of a fool is like the wheel of a cart.
et quasi axis versatilis cogitatus illius.
And his thoughts are like a turning axel.
Equus emissarius, sic et amicus subsannator:
A friend who is a whisperer is like an untamed horse:
he neighs under anyone who sits upon him.
Why does day follow after day,
and year follow after year, in accord with the sun?
By the knowledge of the Lord, they were arranged,
after the sun was made, in keeping with his command.
et in illis dies festos celebraverunt ad horam.
And according to them, they celebrated the feast days, in their hour.
Ex ipsis exaltavit et magnificavit Deus,
Some of them, God exalted and magnified.
et ex ipsis posuit in numerum dierum:
And some of them, he set amid the ordinary days.
et omnes homines de solo et ex terra unde creatus est Adam.
And all men are from the ground, and from the earth, from which Adam was created.
In multitudine disciplinæ Dominus separavit eos,
the Lord has distinguished them and diversified their ways.
And some of them he has sanctified and placed close to himself.
he has cursed and brought low,
et convertit illos a separatione ipsorum.
and he has turned them from their station.
Quasi lutum figuli in manu ipsius,
Just as the clay is in the potter’s hand,
so as to form and to shape it,
Omnes viæ ejus secundum dispositionem ejus:
so are all his ways in accord with his dispensation,
sic homo in manu illius qui se fecit,
and so is man in the hand of the One who made him.
et reddet illi secundum judicium suum.
And he will repay him according to his judgment.
sic et contra virum justum peccator,
so also is a sinner against a just man.
et sic intuere in omnia opera Altissimi,
And so should you consider all the works of the Most High:
And I awakened at the very end,
et quasi qui colligit acinos post vindemiatores.
and I was like one who gathers grapes after the grape-gatherers.
In benedictione Dei et ipse speravi,
I, too, have hoped in the blessing of God.
et quasi qui vindemiat replevi torcular.
And I have filled the winepress like one who gathers grapes.
Respicite quoniam non mihi soli laboravi,
Consider how I have not labored for myself alone,
but for all who are seeking discipline.
You should not give authority over yourself to a son or wife,
non des potestatem super te in vita tua:
et non dederis alii possessionem tuam,
And you should not give your estate to another,
lest perhaps you may regret it,
and then you would be begging for the same.
While you are still living and breathing,
let no one among all flesh change you.
Melius est enim ut filii tui te rogent,
For it is better if your children petition you,
quam te respicere in manus filiorum tuorum.
than if you look toward the hands of your children.
In omnibus operibus tuis præcellens esto.
In all your works, be pre-eminent.
Ne dederis maculam in gloria tua.
You should not allow a blemish upon your glory.
In die consummationis dierum vitæ tuæ,
On the day of the consummation of the days of your life,
at the time of your passing,
and a burden are for a donkey;
and work are for a servant.
Allow his hands to be idle,
Jugum et lorum curvant collum durum,
The yoke and the strap bend a stiff neck,
and continual labors bend a servant.
Torture and chains are for a malevolent servant;
so that he may not be idle.
For idleness has taught much evil.
For this is fitting for him.
And if he will not be obedient,
et non amplifices super omnem carnem:
But you should do no more than any flesh can bear. Truly,
verum sine judicio nihil facias grave.
you should do nothing grievous without judgment.
If you have a faithful servant,
let him be to you like your own soul.
quoniam in sanguine animæ comparasti illum.
For you have obtained him by the blood of your soul.
he will turn away and flee.
And then, when he lifts himself up and departs,
quem quæras et in qua via quæras illum nescis.
you will not know whom to ask, or in what way to seek him.
